historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and Equity 3-year CAGRs elevated due to FY2022 baseline effects (Reality Labs losses, slower growth). FY2025 EPS impacted by $18.9B one-time tax charge. Normalized growth rates suggest 15-20% sustainable revenue growth with FCF temporarily depressed by massive 2026 CapEx cycle ($115-135B guidance).

base.notes: Base case assumes revenue growth decelerating from 15% to 8% as Meta matures. FCF margin of 22% reflects normalization after massive 2026 CapEx cycle. Assumes AI investments drive sustained ad revenue growth, Threads and WhatsApp monetization progresses, and Reality Labs losses stabilize.

bull.notes: Bull case assumes AI-powered advertising dominance drives market share gains, Threads reaches $11B+ revenue potential by year 3, WhatsApp scales to $10B+, and margin expansion from operating leverage. CapEx investments generate strong ROI by year 2-3.

bear.notes: Bear case assumes market share erosion to TikTok and Amazon continues, regulatory fines and compliance costs escalate, massive CapEx fails to generate expected returns, and Reality Labs losses persist longer than expected. FCF margin compressed by infrastructure spending.

base.notes: Base case IV of $375 reflects conservative FCF assumptions during CapEx cycle and moderate growth trajectory.

bull.notes: Bull case assumes successful AI monetization, strong new product revenue (Threads, WhatsApp), and margin expansion.

bear.notes: Bear case reflects market share erosion, CapEx without adequate returns, regulatory pressures, and sustained Reality Labs losses.

base.notes: To achieve 15% CAGR to terminal value per share of $440 over 5 years, entry price would be $219. Current price of $680 implies only 6.8% CAGR to base case terminal value.

bull.notes: Bull case terminal value of $956 requires entry at $475 for 15% CAGR. Current price of $680 implies 7.1% CAGR to bull terminal value.

bear.notes: Bear case terminal value of $254 would require entry at $126 for 15% CAGR.

sensitivity.notes: Sensitivity matrix shows intrinsic value highly sensitive to terminal growth rate assumptions. At current WACC of 10%, IV ranges from $433 (2.5% terminal growth) to $623 (3.5% terminal growth). Current stock price of $680 implies either lower WACC (8-9%) or higher terminal growth (3.5-4%) expectations.

probability_weighted.notes: Probability-weighted IV of $453 applies 30% bull (AI success), 45% base (moderate growth), 25% bear (execution/regulatory risks). Higher bull weighting reflects Meta's strong market position, AI investments, and new monetization opportunities, but elevated bear risk reflects CapEx uncertainty and regulatory headwinds.

capex_sensitivity.description: Meta's massive 2026 CapEx guidance ($115-135B) creates significant near-term FCF pressure but could drive long-term competitive advantages

low_capex_scenario.assumption: CapEx peaks at $115B in 2026, declines to $90B by Y3
low_capex_scenario.impact: FCF increases by ~$15-20B annually from Y2 onward

high_capex_scenario.assumption: CapEx stays elevated at $135B+ through Y3, limited ROI visibility

regulatory_risk_scenarios.status_quo: Current regulatory environment with ongoing compliance costs but no major business model disruption

moderate_impact.description: EU DMA fines escalate to 1-2% of revenue annually, data transfer restrictions require infrastructure duplication
moderate_impact.impact: Operating margin compression of 3-5%, CapEx increased by $5-10B annually

severe_impact.description: EU operations severely curtailed, US federal privacy legislation materially limits ad targeting, TikTok ban reversed strengthening competitor
severe_impact.impact: Revenue growth declines to 5-8%, margin compression of 5-8%
severe_impact.iv_adjustment: -$150-200 per share, approaches bear case valuation

early_success.description: AI advertising tools drive 5-10% pricing power improvement, Meta AI assistant reaches 1B+ users with monetization by Y3
early_success.impact: Revenue growth +3-5pp above base, operating leverage drives margin expansion

delayed_returns.description: AI investments take 5+ years to materially impact financials, competitive positioning stagnant
delayed_returns.impact: Revenue growth in line with base case, but margin expansion delayed 2-3 years

ai_arms_race.description: Competitors match Meta's AI capabilities, preventing differentiation; CapEx becomes table stakes without margin benefit
ai_arms_race.impact: Revenue growth slows to 8-12%, margins compressed by ongoing infrastructure costs

methodology_notes.fcf_definition: Free Cash Flow = Operating Cash Flow - Capital Expenditures. FY2025 FCF of $43.6B = $115.8B operating cash flow - $72.2B CapEx.
methodology_notes.capex_normalization: Base case assumes CapEx as % of revenue declines from peak 2026 levels (~58% of revenue at midpoint $125B guidance on ~$215B revenue) to more normalized 20-25% by Year 3-5. Historical CapEx was 38% in FY2024 and 36% in FY2025.
methodology_notes.reality_labs_treatment: Reality Labs operating losses ($19.2B in FY2025) embedded in consolidated financials. Base case assumes losses stabilize at $18-20B annually before gradual improvement in outer years. Bull case assumes losses begin declining by Year 3. Bear case assumes losses persist at $20B+ through forecast period.
methodology_notes.net_debt_calculation: Net Cash of $22.8B = ($81.6B Cash & Marketable Securities) - ($58.7B Total Debt). Positive value indicates net cash position, which increases equity value in DCF.
methodology_notes.tax_rate_assumptions: FY2025 effective tax rate abnormally high due to $18.9B one-time charge. Normalized tax rate assumed at 18-20% based on historical rates excluding one-time items.
methodology_notes.wacc_derivation: Base case WACC of 10% reflects: risk-free rate ~4.5%, equity risk premium 5.5%, beta 1.0, cost of debt 4.5%, target D/E ratio 10/90. Meta's strong balance sheet and net cash position supports lower WACC vs highly leveraged peers.
methodology_notes.terminal_growth_justification: Terminal growth rate of 3% assumes Meta grows slightly above long-term US GDP growth (2-2.5%) reflecting global exposure, digital advertising growth above GDP, and potential new business lines (AR/VR, AI products). Conservative vs historical growth given maturation and competitive dynamics.

current_valuation_metrics.notes: Current valuation of 29x P/E and 40x P/FCF reflects premium pricing for growth and AI opportunity, but near-term FCF multiple inflated by CapEx cycle.

historical_valuation_context.current_vs_historical: Trading 28% above historical average P/E multiple
historical_valuation_context.notes: Current valuation premium justified by AI investment thesis and improved revenue growth trajectory, but downside risk if execution disappoints or macro deteriorates.

peer_comparison.meta_position: META trades at premium to Alphabet (20x P/E) and inline with smaller social media peers. However, Meta's scale, profitability, and FCF generation are superior.
peer_comparison.notes: Peer multiples: Alphabet 20x P/E, Snap 45x P/E (unprofitable), Pinterest 35x P/E, Reddit 180x P/E (growth mode). Meta's 29x P/E appears reasonable given growth + profitability profile.

investment_conclusion.rationale: At $680 per share, META appears modestly overvalued versus base case IV of $375 and probability-weighted IV of $453. Stock price implies bull case assumptions (successful AI monetization, strong new product revenue, margin expansion) are largely priced in. Near-term risks include: (1) massive CapEx cycle depressing FCF through 2026-2027, (2) regulatory uncertainty particularly in EU, (3) market share erosion to TikTok and Amazon, (4) uncertain AI investment ROI timeline.
investment_conclusion.upside_scenarios: Stock could work if: (1) Threads and WhatsApp monetization exceeds expectations ($15-20B+ combined revenue by 2027-2028), (2) AI tools drive market share gains and pricing power, (3) Reality Labs losses decline faster than expected, (4) CapEx yields early wins by late 2026/early 2027 enabling management to moderate spending plans.
investment_conclusion.downside_risks: Significant downside to $450-550 range if: (1) CapEx fails to generate expected returns and must remain elevated through 2027+, (2) EU regulatory actions escalate to material revenue/profit impact, (3) ad market softens due to recession, (4) competition from TikTok and AI-powered alternatives intensifies.
investment_conclusion.recommendation: Current valuation leaves limited margin of safety. Better entry point would be $500-550 range (20-25x forward P/E) which would offer 15%+ upside to probability-weighted IV. For existing holders, maintain position given long-term optionality but trim on strength above $700. For new positions, wait for pullback or conviction that AI investments are generating tangible ROI.
